title: Philip III to the Count of Añover, Lerma, 20 May 1610 (Madrid, Biblioteca Histórica Municipal, I 242,29): a partial nomenclator rebuilt from sibling letters (catalogue 1988)

documents.shelfmark: Madrid, Biblioteca Histórica Municipal (Ayuntamiento de Madrid), I 242,29 (Memoria de Madrid 424541; Hispana idBib 58678726)
documents.route: Philip III (Lerma) -> Rodrigo Niño Laso, conde de Añover

plaintext.source: Real cédula in cipher; no decipherment bound in or with it (catalogue 1988: four leaves of the series have none). The key values come from the clear texts of the sibling letters I 242,33, 42, 47 and 48.

transcription.source: Alberto Garvía García's report (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.24174363, section 4): ten lines of f. 53r; the five pages were transcribed in full in his dossier (not seen here); images from Memoria de Madrid
transcription.notes: The 211 cipher-group occurrences are the contributor's segmentation figure; the ten lines were not counted by the project with the measure tool because the signs are typographic approximations (delta, R, B, ji, a loop). Not checked against the manuscript images (403 from Memoria de Madrid).

system.summary: A mixed nomenclator: numbers 10 to 114 and 241-242 with letter-syllable signs (ba, cle, je, fal, ...), homophones for letters, syllables and whole words, groups of unequal length, nulls likely; rebuilt by the contributor from sibling letters; no key sheet of the series has been identified.
system.sibling_key: I 242,33, 42, 47 and 48 (clear text in the same volume); I 242,71 as a separate control, not transferred

prior_solution.where: No reading of I 242,29 known: the contributor searched Tomokiyo, DECODE, Retortillo Atienza 2019 and the Correia thesis; a web search here found none. Devos 1950 not consulted.

conditions.human_role: Alberto Garvía García directed the work and posted it; the transcription, matching with the sibling clear texts and the key table were prepared with ChatGPT/Codex (his statement). No independent palaeographic check. This project checked the report and re-derived the reading from his transcription and key table with its own parser; the manuscripts could not be fetched.

solution.what: The contributor obtained images of I 242,29 and the siblings I 242,33, 42, 47, 48 and 71 from Memoria de Madrid; the images of 47 and 48 reached him by a user's contribution (his report). The project's own requests to the viewer returned 403.

Sequences of the ciphers of I 242,42, 47, 48 and 33 matched with their contemporary clear texts to give group values (66 graded C, 3 M, 5 I in the table for I 242,29); I 242,71 kept apart as a negative control (the earlier key is not transferred).

Ten lines of f. 53r read in part: Dutch factory at Pinda, Angola coast, against the truce; the king charges the count to see it remedied and report. The contributor's figures: 173 of 211 group occurrences in firm words (81.99%), 202 of 211 with an equivalence in the table (95.73%), 78 of 88 words firm.

Own parser applied to the transcription and key table of the report (all segmentations of the digit runs): 213 tokens, two not in the table as written; the output is the contributor's reading, ten lines of connected Spanish. The transcription and the sibling parallels are not checked against the manuscripts.

Control of my own, Spanish 1490-1650 quadgrams on the decode against 200 permutations of the digit values: real -4.39 per letter, best permutation -4.20: inconclusive on this short syllabic text; not relied on. The contributor's own control was not re-run.

Prior art: Tomokiyo, DECODE, Retortillo Atienza 2019 and Correia searched by the contributor; a web search here found no mention of a 1610 cipher letter to Añover about Pinda; Devos 1950 not consulted.

English translation contributed by Alberto Garvía García (PR #547, translation.md): line by line on reading.md, the same 12 bracketed holes in the same lines and order (checked by script), no claim of a complete decipherment. Two small fixes here: line 1 'it has been learned [101: report?]' put back as 'word [101: report?] has been had' so the bracketed code is not translated twice; line 5 the null 58~ restored in its place inside 'stipu-la[58~: null?]ted' with its gloss.

Issue #499 comments of 13 Nov 2026: the contributor's 211-token analytical layer and his control windows A01-D06, E01-E04 saved in contributor/; all 211 tokens have a value in key.tsv and decode to his reading letter for letter; the 74-entry graded table equals key.tsv. Dudout's independent transcription comparison (all digit strings of L01-L10 agree; L05 bo/60 doubtful) recorded. Memoria de Madrid still 403, images not seen. No open code closed; strict share unchanged (88.6%).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The contributor rebuilt a partial nomenclator from the clear texts of sibling letters in the same volume (I 242,33, 42, 47, 48) and applied it to I 242,29, whose cipher has no decipherment bound in. The reading reproduces from his transcription and table; the manuscripts and the sibling plaintexts were not seen by the project, and the transcription is unverified.

credits.note: posted the key table, the transcription and the reading of I 242,29 (report on Zenodo, doi 10.5281/zenodo.24174363; ChatGPT/Codex-assisted, as he states)
independent transcription of I 242,29 f. 53r (3 Nov 2026, by his record) agrees on every digit string; L05 bo/60 doubt; pointed to I 243,18 and I 242,35/59/60

outcome.fraction_read_source: The contributor's own word count (report, section 7): 78 of 88 words firm = 88.6%; firm means every value in the word is graded C (matched with a clear text), as strict as the README rule. Not recomputed word by word; his looser figures (173 of 211 group occurrences = 81.99%; 202 of 211 with a table equivalence = 95.73%) are not the read bar.
outcome.notes: In progress. Ten lines of f. 53r read in part from a key rebuilt from sibling letters; transcription and sibling parallels unchecked against the images (Memoria de Madrid blocked scripted requests). No page.

texts.label: Philip III to the Count of Añover, 20 May 1610 (I 242,29): the ten transcribed lines
texts.summary: Philip III learns that Dutch merchants are setting up a factory at Pinda on the coast of Angola, against the truce, and charges the Count of Añover to remedy it without sending anyone to the Islands, and to report.
